question.text: Moment of inertia of a disc of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> and radius '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>' about any of its diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>M</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>. The moment of inertia of this disc about an axis normal to the disc and passing through a point on its edge will be, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>M</mi><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Given here, 

Moment of inertia of a disc of mass M and radius 'R' about any of its diameter is MR24. 

Moment of inertia of disc about centre is Icm=MR24+MR24=MR22

Using parallel axis theorem, we can write

I=Icm+Md2

=MR22+MR2

=32MR2

Hence, the value of x=3.
